Reviews summary aggregation & date filters - pass - evidence: /reviews/summary distribution sums == total; rating=5 filter -> only 5-star counts; future date -> total=0; /reviews list date_from/date_to narrow correctly to that day.

Frontend Download Sheet dropdown (xlsx + csv) - pass - evidence: Playwright triggered both live-export-xlsx and live-export-csv from live-export dropdown; both produced real download events with expected extensions (.xlsx / .csv) and filenames derived from app name + filters.

Frontend filters + reset + empty state - pass - evidence: star-5 changed Reviews (filtered) 100 -> 54; live-reset cleared filters; live-from=2099-01-01/live-to=2099-12-31 rendered 'No reviews match these filters'.

minor.issue: Dedup by review-id is correct, but Google Play public scraper returns slightly different 40-item windows between rapid consecutive requests, so a naive assertion 'imported=0 on 2nd sync' is flaky. In practice 38/40 (95%) dedup'd on the 2nd sync in this run and 100% is not guaranteed for live data. Consider (a) documenting this in the test, or (b) sync with a larger max_count and assert skipped >= 90% instead of imported==0.

critical_code_review_comments: routes_reviews.export_reviews: openpyxl writes the entire workbook into memory (bio) before returning. For 20000-row workbooks this can easily exceed 20-30MB and hold peak memory. Fine at current scale (100-500 rows) but a StreamingResponse with WriteOnlyWorkbook + write_only=True mode would be preferable for the truncated ceiling.

routes_reviews._date_range still mixes '00:00:00' (naive) for date_from and '+00:00' offset for date_to — carry-over from prior iteration. Because reviews.created_at strings from now_iso() are tz-aware ISO, the string comparison happens to work but is fragile if a legacy naive record ever appears.

providers.get_provider swaps GooglePlayProvider (raises NotConnectedError) for GooglePlayLiveProvider when credentials are absent — this is the correct 'live-read fallback' pattern. However GooglePlayProvider.fetch_reviews raises unconditionally even when service_account_json is present because the method body is still a stub; the current code path is only ever selected via the sync endpoint when creds are set, so this is effectively unreachable until real creds land, but the class-level docstring should call this out to prevent surprise.

LiveReviews.jsx exportSheet uses fmt as both blob mime resolver and filename extension — the .xlsx / .csv discrimination is centralised, good. Only nit: no per-row-count spinner in dropdown item (Excel large exports may pause 1-2s before download).

test_gplay_live.py::test_sync_dedupes_on_repeat asserts imported==0 which is too strict for Google Play public data (see minor backend issue). Recommend softening to 'skipped_duplicates >= 0.9 * fetched'.
